A2AAgentCreateRequest.description: Registration parameters for a new A2A agent.

allow_insecure_oauth_http.description: Allow non-loopback HTTP OAuth discovery/metadata endpoints for this agent instead of requiring HTTPS. Defaults to false.

allow_insecure_tls_skip_verify.description: Skip TLS certificate verification when connecting to this agent's endpoint (self-signed/private certs). Defaults to false.

auth_config.description: Authentication config key-values, e.g. the API key or bearer token. Values under credential-looking keys (name containing KEY, SECRET, TOKEN, PASSWORD, etc.) are masked back in responses.

auth_mode.description: Authentication mode: `shared` (default) shares one credential across all users; `per_user_secret` requires `secret_schema.header_name`; `per_user_oauth` runs per-user OAuth.

auth_type.description: Authentication type for reaching the remote agent: `none` (default when omitted), `api_key`, or `bearer`.

card_url.description: URL of the remote agent card. Must be an absolute `http` or `https` URL with a non-empty host; reachability is enforced by the execution environment, not at creation time.

environments.description: Execution environments this agent is callable from: `cloud` and/or BYOC runner environment IDs. Omitted or empty means all environments.

instructions.description: Natural-language instructions for the remote agent: a Markdown document with optional `summary` frontmatter and a non-empty body, at most 50 KiB (51200 bytes). Required — a deprecated `description` field is still accepted for legacy clients and, if both are sent, must exactly match `instructions`.

oauth_metadata.description: JSON-encoded OAuth metadata; populated by the OAuth discovery flow for `per_user_oauth` mode.

secret_schema.description: JSON-encoded secret schema, e.g. `{"header_name":"X-Api-Key"}`; required when `auth_mode=per_user_secret`.

streaming.description: Whether the remote agent supports streaming.

team_id.description: Team scope: 0 = account-wide; >0 = team. Creating at account scope requires the owner/admin role; creating into a team requires actual membership in that team.

A2AAgentCreateResponse.description: Result of registering an A2A agent.

agent_id.description: ID of the newly created agent.

agent_card_name.description: Agent name resolved from the remote card. Omitted until the card has been fetched.

agent_card_skills.description: Skills advertised by the remote card. Omitted until the card has been fetched.

allow_insecure_oauth_http.description: Allow non-loopback HTTP OAuth discovery/metadata endpoints for this agent instead of requiring HTTPS.

allow_insecure_tls_skip_verify.description: Skip TLS certificate verification when connecting to this agent's endpoint.

auth_config.description: Authentication config key-values. Values under credential-looking keys (name containing KEY, SECRET, TOKEN, PASSWORD, etc.) are masked. Omitted when empty.

auth_mode.description: Authentication mode. One of: `shared` (a single static credential saved on the resource and shared by all callers in the account; the default — an empty value behaves the same), `per_user_secret` (each user stores their own secret per `secret_schema`, injected per user at runtime), `per_user_oauth` (each user completes their own OAuth grant; discovery and registration run lazily on first use).

auth_type.description: Authentication type for reaching the remote agent: `none`, `api_key`, or `bearer`. Rows created before validation was tightened may return an empty string, equivalent to `none`.

can_edit.description: Whether the caller may edit this agent.

card_resolve_timeout.description: Card-resolution timeout in seconds. Always 0 today — the API does not yet expose a way to set it.

card_url.description: URL of the remote agent card.

created_at.description: Creation time. Unix timestamp in milliseconds.

created_by.description: Member ID that created the agent.

environments.description: Execution environments this agent is callable from (`cloud` and/or BYOC runner environment IDs). Always present; `[]` means all environments (also the value on legacy rows created before this field).

instructions.description: Natural-language instructions for the remote agent (formerly named `description`).

status.description: Agent status.

streaming.description: Whether the remote agent supports streaming responses.

task_timeout.description: Single-task execution timeout in seconds. Always 0 today — the API does not yet expose a way to set it.

team_id.description: Team scope: 0 = account-wide; >0 = the owning team.

updated_at.description: Last update time. Unix timestamp in milliseconds.

A2AAgentListRequest.description: Pagination, scope, and search filter for listing A2A agents.

include_account.description: Include account-scoped (team_id=0) rows. Defaults to true.

offset.description: Pagination offset — number of rows to skip, starting from 0.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring search across agent name, instructions, card URL, agent ID, and the resolved card name.

scope.description: Visibility scope: `all` (account-scope plus the caller's visible teams), `account` (account-scope only), or `team` (team-scoped rows across the caller's visible teams).

team_ids.description: Filter to these team IDs; empty = the caller's visible set.

items.description: A2A agents on this page.

A2AAgentUpdateRequest.description: Partial update of an A2A agent. A null/omitted field is left unchanged.

agent_id.description: Target agent ID, from the list returned by `POST /safari/a2a-agent/list`.

agent_name.description: New display name. Omit to leave unchanged.

allow_insecure_oauth_http.description: Toggle non-loopback HTTP OAuth discovery for this agent. Omit to leave unchanged.

allow_insecure_tls_skip_verify.description: Toggle TLS certificate verification skipping for this agent. Omit to leave unchanged.

auth_config.description: Replace the whole auth config; omit to leave unchanged. Keys missing from the map are dropped. For a sensitive key, sending back the masked value keeps the stored secret, while sending an empty string clears it.

auth_mode.description: New auth mode: shared, per_user_secret, or per_user_oauth. Changing it always rewrites secret_schema together with it.

auth_type.description: New auth type: `none`, `api_key`, or `bearer`. Omit to leave unchanged.

card_url.description: New card URL. Omit to leave unchanged.

environments.description: Execution environments this agent is callable from: `cloud` and/or BYOC runner environment IDs. Omit (null) to leave unchanged; send a list to set it — an empty list clears the restriction back to all environments.

instructions.description: New instructions document (same contract as create: optional `summary` frontmatter, non-empty body, at most 50 KiB). Omit to leave unchanged. A deprecated `description` field is also accepted; if both are sent they must match.

oauth_metadata.description: New JSON OAuth metadata. If omitted while auth_mode changes, it is cleared to empty.

streaming.description: Toggle streaming support. Omit to leave unchanged.

team_id.description: Reassign team scope. Omit to leave unchanged. Reassigning requires rights on the destination team; if the team changes without also sending a new environment binding, the existing runner binding must remain selectable by the caller or the update is rejected.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 region code of the contact phone (e.g. "CN", "US", "HK").

created_at.description: Account creation time, Unix timestamp in seconds.

mp_account_id.description: Account identifier on the marketplace platform. Omitted together with `mp_plat`.

mp_plat.description: Cloud marketplace platform the account was provisioned from. Omitted when the account did not come from a marketplace.

phone.description: Account contact phone, masked for privacy.

restrictions.description: Account access restrictions. Omitted when none are configured.

allow_subdomain.description: Whether subdomains of the allowed email domains are also accepted.

time_zone.description: Account default timezone (IANA name, e.g. Asia/Shanghai).

AckIncidentRequest.description: Parameters for acknowledging one or more incidents.

custom_fields.description: Custom field values for the acknowledgement form. Allowed keys and values depend on the incident's visible form.

images.description: Images attached to the acknowledgement timeline entry.

incident_ids.description: Incident IDs to acknowledge. At most 100 per call.

summary.description: Form summary recorded as a timeline comment. Accepted only when the acknowledgement form contains a summary element.

AddIncidentResponderRequest.description: Parameters for adding responders to an existing incident.

notify.description: Optional notification override. Defaults to following each person's personal preference.

follow_preference.description: When false, use `personal_channels`; when true or omitted, use each responder's personal preference.

template_id.description: Notification template ID (MongoDB ObjectID).

person_ids.description: Member IDs to add as responders.

chat_id.description: Chat ID of the war room within the IM platform.

integration_id.description: ID of the IM integration hosting the war room; obtain it from `POST /datasource/im/war-room-enabled/list`.

member_ids.description: Person IDs to add to the war room.

AffectedStatusPageComponentItem.description: A status page component currently affected by an event, embedding component metadata plus its resulting status.

available_since_seconds.description: Time the component became available, as a Unix timestamp in seconds. Omitted when 0.

hide_all.description: When true, the component is hidden entirely from summary endpoints. Omitted when false.

hide_uptime.description: When true, uptime data is hidden from summary responses. Omitted when false.

order_id.description: Display order within its section. Omitted when 0.

section_id.description: Parent section ID. Omitted when the component sits at the top level.

status.description:
Current status of the component affected by the change. Severity increases: `operational` < `degraded` = `under_maintenance` < `partial_outage` < `full_outage`; incident-type changes may use the first four, maintenance-type changes only `operational` and `under_maintenance`.
| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `operational` | Operating normally. |
| `degraded` | Degraded performance. |
| `partial_outage` | Partial outage. |
| `full_outage` | Full outage. |
| `under_maintenance` | Under maintenance. |

channel_ids.description: Filter by channel IDs. At most 100 entries.

end_time.description: End of the search window, Unix epoch seconds. Must be greater than `start_time` when provided.

orderby.description: Sort field; only `event_time` is supported.

p.description: Page number, starting at 1. Used when `search_after_ctx` is not provided.

search_after_ctx.description: Pagination cursor: leave empty for the first page, then pass the `search_after_ctx` returned by the previous response.

severities.description: Comma-separated severity filter, e.g. `Critical,Warning`. Accepted values: `Critical`, `Warning`, `Info`, `Ok`.

start_time.description: Start of the search window, Unix epoch seconds. Must be greater than 0 when provided.

has_next_page.description: Whether a next page exists (probed by fetching limit+1 rows).

items.description: Raw alert events on the current page.

search_after_ctx.description: Cursor for the next page — the ObjectID of the last event on this page; pass it back as `search_after_ctx`. Omitted when the page is empty; in cursor mode also omitted when there is no next page.

alert_key.description: Deduplication key used to merge events into an alert.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete time, Unix epoch seconds. Omitted when the event is not deleted.

event_status.description: Status carried by this event: `Critical`/`Warning`/`Info` for a firing event, `Ok` for a recovery event.

integration_id.description: Integration that produced this event.

updated_at.description: Record update time, Unix epoch seconds.

asc.description: When true, return events oldest-first. Defaults to newest-first.

limit.description: Page size. Defaults to 20 and cannot exceed 100.

has_next_page.description: Whether another page is available.

items.description: Raw alert events in the requested order.

search_after_ctx.description: Cursor to pass as `search_after_ctx` for the next page. Omitted when the page is empty; in cursor mode also omitted when there is no next page.

total.description: Total matching event count, capped at 1000.

alert_id.description: Alert ID (ObjectID hex string); obtain it from `POST /alert/list`.

AlertFeedType.description:
Alert activity feed entry type. Each value identifies one alert lifecycle event; the matching `detail` payload shape is determined by this field.

| Type | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `a_new` | Alert triggered by an incoming event. |
| `a_update` | Alert severity or status changed on an incoming event. |
| `a_comm` | Comment added on the alert. |
| `a_merge` | Alert merged into an incident. |
| `a_m_silence` | Alert muted by a silence rule. |
| `a_m_inhibit` | Alert muted by an inhibit rule. |
| `a_m_flapping` | Alert muted by flapping detection (historical data only; no longer produced). |
| `a_ack` | Alert acknowledged (historical data only; alert-level acknowledgement has been removed). |
| `a_unack` | Alert acknowledgement revoked (historical data only). |
| `a_close` | Alert closed (historical data only; no longer produced). |

alert_status.description: Current status: `Critical`/`Warning`/`Info` while firing, `Ok` once recovered.

AlertListRequest.description: Filter and pagination criteria for alert list queries. Time range is required.

alert_ids.description: Filter to specific alert IDs (ObjectID hex strings). Invalid IDs are ignored; if none are valid, the result is empty.

alert_severity.description: Comma-separated severity filter, e.g. `Critical,Warning`. Allowed values: `Critical`, `Warning`, `Info`, `Ok`.

asc.description: Sort ascending by `start_time` when `true`; default is descending.

by_updated_at.description: When `true`, the time range filter is applied on `updated_at` rather than `start_time`.

end_time.description: End of the search window, Unix epoch seconds. Must be greater than `start_time`; the span must not exceed 31 days and must lie within the account's data retention period.

ever_muted.description: Filter by whether the alert has ever been silenced.

is_active.description: Filter by lifecycle: `true` returns only firing alerts (status `Critical`/`Warning`/`Info`), `false` returns only recovered alerts (status `Ok`). Omit or pass `null` to return both.

p.description: Page number, starting at 1. Used when `search_after_ctx` is not provided; `p * limit` must stay within 10,000 records.

search_after_ctx.description: Opaque cursor from the previous response for the next page.

start_time.description: Start of the search window, Unix epoch seconds.

has_next_page.description: True if more pages are available.

items.description: Alerts on the current page.

search_after_ctx.description: Cursor for the next page — the ObjectID hex of the last alert on this page; pass it back as `search_after_ctx`. Present only when `has_next_page` is true.

alert_ids.description: Alert IDs to merge (ObjectID hex strings); obtain them from `POST /alert/list`. Every ID must belong to the caller's account.

comment.description: Optional comment recorded on the merge feed entry. At most 1024 characters.

incident_id.description: Target incident ID (ObjectID hex string); obtain it from `POST /incident/list`.

owner_id.description: Member ID of the new owner for the target incident; obtain it from `POST /member/list`.

title.description: Optional new title for the target incident. At most 512 characters.

if.description: AND-filter list — the rule applies only when every condition matches. `null` or omitted means the rule applies to all events.

kind.description:
Rule type. Rules run in array order; when the `if` condition matches, the event is processed according to `kind`.
| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `title_reset` | Rewrites the event title from the `settings.title` template. |
| `description_reset` | Rewrites the event description from the `settings.description` template. |
| `severity_reset` | Resets the event severity and status to `settings.severity` (`Critical`/`Warning`/`Info`). |
| `alert_drop` | Discards the matching event outright; no alert is created. |
| `alert_inhibit` | Discards the event (inhibition) when an active source alert matching `settings.source_filters` and correlated via `settings.equals` exists. |

settings.description:
Kind-specific settings. Shape depends on `kind`:
- `title_reset`: `{ "title": "<string>" }`
- `description_reset`: `{ "description": "<string>" }`
- `severity_reset`: `{ "severity": "Critical"|"Warning"|"Info" }`
- `alert_drop`: `{}` (empty object)
- `alert_inhibit`: `{ "equals": ["<label_key>", ...], "source_filters": <OrFilterGroup> }`

integration_id.description: Integration ID. Must be greater than 0.

AlertPipelineItem.description: Alert processing pipeline for an integration.

created_at.description: Creation timestamp, Unix epoch seconds.

creator_id.description: Member ID who created the pipeline.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete time, Unix epoch seconds. Omitted when not deleted.

integration_id.description: Integration ID this pipeline applies to.

status.description: Pipeline status. Always `enabled` in these responses — deleted pipelines are filtered out.

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp, Unix epoch seconds.

updated_by.description: Member ID who last updated the pipeline.

integration_ids.description: Integration IDs. At least one entry is required.

items.description: Alert pipeline configuration of each requested integration, one item per configured integration.

integration_id.description: Integration ID to configure.

rules.description: Rules to apply, evaluated in array order. Between 1 and 50 entries.

account_id.description: Account ID. Filled by the server from the authenticated identity; do not provide.

annotations.description: Annotation key-value pairs delivered with alert events; keys must not start with `$` (reserved for query fields).

channel_ids.description: Channel IDs to send alerts to.

created_at.description: Creation time as a Unix timestamp in seconds. Generated by the server; do not provide.

creator_id.description: Creator user ID. Filled by the server from the current user; do not provide.

creator_name.description: Creator name. Filled by the server; do not provide.

cron_pattern.description: Schedule expression: a 6-field cron (with seconds) or an `@every 30s` interval descriptor. Must not start with `CRON_TZ=` or `TZ=`; use the `timezone` field instead.

debug_log_enabled.description: Whether to enable debug logging; the edge emits detailed evaluation logs, useful for troubleshooting rules that do not trigger as expected.

delay_seconds.description: Seconds to shift the evaluation query window backward, compensating for data ingestion latency.

description_type.description: Format for the description. Defaults to `text` when omitted or empty. `text` = plain text; `markdown` = Markdown, rendered as Markdown in alert details.

ds_ids.description: Datasource IDs, merged with `ds_list` to decide which datasources the rule monitors; IDs survive datasource renames. At least one of `ds_list` and `ds_ids` must be provided.

ds_list.description: Data source name patterns (supports wildcards). At least one of `ds_list` / `ds_ids` must be non-empty; the two are merged to decide which datasources the rule monitors.

ds_type.description: Datasource type identifier; allowed values are listed by `POST /monit/rule/dstypes` (e.g. `prometheus`, `elasticsearch`).

enabled.description: Whether the rule is enabled. Updating to `false` makes the server clean up the rule's active alerts.

enabled_times.description: Time windows when the rule is active. Defaults to all days from 00:00 to 23:59 when omitted or empty.

folder_id.description: ID of the folder the rule belongs to. Obtainable via `POST /monit/folder/list`.

id.description: Rule ID. Required for update; omit for create (assigned by the server).

name.description: Rule name. Must be unique within the same folder.

rule_configs.description: Check configuration: query list plus trigger/recovery conditions. Structure see `RuleConfigs`.

timezone.description: Timezone in which the rule executes. Determines how the cron schedule and effective time windows are interpreted. Only IANA timezone names are accepted (e.g. `Asia/Shanghai`, `UTC`, `Europe/London`); shortcuts and offsets such as `Local`, `UTC+8`, or `CST` are rejected. Treated as `Asia/Shanghai` if empty.

updated_at.description: Last update time as a Unix timestamp in seconds. Generated by the server; do not provide.

updater_id.description: Last updater user ID. Filled by the server; do not provide.

updater_name.description: Last updater name. Filled by the server; do not provide.

AlertRuleAudit.description: An audit record capturing a rule snapshot at a point in time.

account_id.description: ID of the account that owns the rule.

action.description: Action performed: `create` = rule created; `update` = rule updated (covers full updates, field-batch updates, imports and moves).

alert_rule_id.description: ID of the alert rule this record belongs to.

content.description: JSON string of the full rule snapshot at audit time. Populated on `/monit/rule/audit/detail`, omitted on list responses.

created_at.description: When this audit record was produced, as a Unix timestamp in seconds; equals the rule's `updated_at` at change time.

creator_id.description: ID of the user who made this change (taken from the rule's `updater_id` at change time).

creator_name.description: Name of the user who made this change (taken from the rule's `updater_name` at change time).

id.description: Audit record ID.

AlertRuleBasic.description: Basic alert rule information for list views.

active_alert_count.description: Number of currently active (unrecovered) alerts fired by this rule. `triggered` equals `active_alert_count > 0`.

created_at.description: Creation time, as a Unix timestamp in seconds.

creator_id.description: ID of the user who created the rule.

creator_name.description: Name of the user who created the rule.

cron_pattern.description: Schedule expression: a 6-field cron with seconds, e.g. `0 * * * * *`, or an `@every 30s` interval descriptor. Must not start with `CRON_TZ=` or `TZ=`; use the `timezone` field instead.

enabled.description: Whether the rule is enabled.

id.description: Unique rule ID.

runtime_state.description:
Runtime evaluation state, derived from edge heartbeats and the edge-reported rule status. Omitted when the state is unavailable.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `disabled` | The rule is disabled. |
| `offline` | The edge instance or cluster owning this rule is offline. |
| `abnormal` | The edge reports evaluation errors. |
| `stale` | The edge's runtime status report is outdated. |
| `no_datasource` | No datasource currently matches the rule's `ds_list` / `ds_ids`. |
| `config_pending` | The latest rule config has not been delivered to the edge yet. |
| `waiting` | Enabled, but the edge has not reported runtime status yet. |
| `normal` | Evaluating normally. |

timezone.description: Timezone in which the rule executes. Determines how the cron schedule and effective time windows are interpreted. Only IANA timezone names are accepted (e.g. `Asia/Shanghai`, `UTC`, `Europe/London`); shortcuts and offsets such as `Local`, `UTC+8`, or `CST` are rejected. Treated as `Asia/Shanghai` if empty.

triggered.description: True if the rule currently has active alerts.

updated_at.description: Last modification time, as a Unix timestamp in seconds.

updater_id.description: ID of the user who last modified the rule.

updater_name.description: Name of the user who last modified the rule.

AlertRuleCounter.description: One historical snapshot of the account's alert rule total.

account_id.description: ID of the account this snapshot belongs to.

id.description: ID of this snapshot record.

num.description: Rule count at the sample time.

AlertRuleExport.description: Portable alert rule representation for import/export. Omits identifying fields like `id`, `account_id`, and audit metadata.

annotations.description: Custom annotation key-value pairs attached to alert events; keys must not start with `$` (reserved for query field references).

cron_pattern.description: Evaluation schedule as a 6-field cron expression (seconds included) or `@every <duration>` (an integral number of seconds, at least 1s); `CRON_TZ=`/`TZ=` prefixes are rejected — set the timezone in `timezone` instead.

debug_log_enabled.description: Whether to emit debug logs for this rule's evaluations; enable when troubleshooting.

delay_seconds.description: Query time offset in seconds: each evaluation reads data as of `schedule time − delay_seconds` to tolerate ingestion lag; `0` means no offset.

description.description: Rule description in the format given by `description_type`, shown with alert events.

description_type.description: Format of `description`, `text` or `markdown`; treated as `text` when omitted.

ds_ids.description: Datasource ID list, merged with `ds_list`; references by ID and is therefore immune to datasource renames.

ds_list.description: Datasource name list with wildcard support; merged with `ds_ids` to decide which datasources the rule monitors — must be maintained by hand if a datasource is renamed.

ds_type.description: Datasource type ident, e.g. `prometheus`; must be a datasource type (`ident`) that exists in the import target environment.

enabled.description: Whether the rule is enabled; rules imported as disabled are not evaluated.

enabled_times.description: Effective time windows; each entry has `days` (0–6, 0 = Sunday) and `stime`/`etime` (`HH:MM`), interpreted in the rule's `timezone`; an empty list disables the rule.

labels.description: Custom label key-value pairs attached to alert events produced by this rule.

name.description: Rule name, up to 128 characters when imported.

repeat_interval.description: Interval in seconds between repeated notifications for a firing alert; values below 1 fall back to the default of 3600.

repeat_total.description: Maximum number of repeated notifications for the same alert; values below 1 fall back to the default of 3.

timezone.description: Timezone in which the rule executes. IANA timezone name; defaults to `Asia/Shanghai`.

status.description:
Run status. One of (the first three are in-flight, the rest terminal):
| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `queued` | Enqueued, waiting for a worker |
| `running` | Executing |
| `retrying` | An attempt failed and a retry is scheduled |
| `succeeded` | Completed successfully |
| `partial` | Partially succeeded (currently only produced by memory-consolidation runs; rule runs never reach it) |
| `failed` | Terminal failure, no further retries |
| `skipped` | Not executed (e.g. grace period expired, trigger or rule invalid); the reason is kept on the run record |
| `abandoned` | Still in-flight past the stale threshold and swept as never-completed (e.g. worker died) |
| `blocked` | Terminal: the run produced output but ended with a connector waiting on a human to complete authorization (distinct from `failed`) |

trigger_kind.description:
Trigger kind. One of:
| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `schedule` | Fired by the rule's schedule trigger |
| `debug` | Debug run (reserved; current rule runs never carry this kind) |
| `manual` | Triggered manually by a user |
| `http_post` | Fired via the rule's HTTP POST webhook |
| `oncall_incident` | Fired by an on-call incident event |

auto_resolve_timeout.description: Auto-resolve timeout in seconds. 0 disables auto-resolve. Max 30 days.

escalate_rule.description: Default escalation rule applied to the channel. Omit to skip default escalation.

aggr_window.description: Delay window in seconds. 0 disables delay.

target.description: Notification target. At least one of `person_ids`, `team_ids`, `schedule_to_role_ids`, or `emails` must be set, together with either `by` or `webhooks`.

by.description: Per-severity personal notification channels. Required unless `webhooks` is provided.

critical.description: Notify channels used for Critical severity. Personal channels: `sms`, `voice`, `email`, `push`; IM group-chat channels: `feishu_app:<chat_id>`, `dingtalk_app:<chat_id>`, `wecom_app:<chat_id>`, `slack_app:<chat_id>`, `teams_app:<chat_id>`.

follow_preference.description: When true, use each responder's personal preference instead of the lists below.

info.description: Notify channels used for Info severity. Values as for `critical`.

warning.description: Notify channels used for Warning severity. Values as for `critical`.

person_ids.description: Member IDs to notify directly; obtain member IDs from `POST /member/list`.

schedule_to_role_ids.description: Map of schedule ID to the role IDs on that schedule to notify.

team_ids.description: Team IDs to notify; obtain team IDs from `POST /team/list`.

webhooks.description: Group chat / webhook targets. Required unless `by` is provided.

type.description: Webhook type, one of `feishu`, `feishu_app`, `dingtalk`, `dingtalk_app`, `wecom`, `slack`, `slack_app`, `teams_app`, `telegram`, `zoom`.

template_id.description: Notification template ID (MongoDB ObjectID).

event_group.description: Alert event merge configuration. Omit to use the default (merge enabled, 1440-minute window).

mute_mins.description: Mute duration in minutes after flapping is detected.

all_equals_required.description: When true, all listed keys must be present for grouping.

items.description: Conditional grouping override: stored alerts matching `if` are grouped by `equals` instead of the top-level grouping keys.

equals.description: Grouping keys for matching alerts. Supported values: `title`, `description`, `severity`, or any `labels.<name>`.

if.description: AND-ed match conditions evaluated against stored alert fields.

equals.description: Groups of label keys whose equality defines a bucket.

i_keys.description: Label keys used for intelligent grouping embeddings.

time_window.description: Grouping time window in minutes. Default max is 1440 minutes (24 h); extended accounts may allow up to 43200 minutes (30 days).

window_type.description: Window type, default `tumbling`. `tumbling` is a fixed window counted from incident creation — once it expires, new alerts open a new incident; `sliding` is a sliding window counted from the incident's most recent alert, extended each time a new alert merges in.

is_external_report_enabled.description: Allow external reporters to file incidents into this channel.

is_private.description: When true, the channel is visible only to its managing teams.

managing_team_ids.description: Additional teams that can manage the channel. Up to 3 entries.

plugin_ids.description: IDs of plugins (integrations) subscribed to this channel.

team_id.description: Owning team ID; obtain it from `POST /team/list`.

CreateDropRuleRequest.description: Parameters for creating a channel drop rule.

channel_id.description: Owning channel ID; obtain it from `POST /channel/list`.

filters.description: Alert event match conditions (OR-of-AND); matching events are discarded entirely — no alert, incident, or notification is produced. When omitted or empty, the rule matches nothing.

CreateEscalationRuleRequest.description: Parameters for creating an escalation rule.

aggr_window.description: Delay window in seconds. 0 disables delay.

channel_id.description: Owning channel ID; obtain it from `POST /channel/list`.

filters.description: Incident-level match conditions (OR-of-AND tree): the rule is matched against the incident the alert was grouped into, not against the alert itself. Omit or leave empty to apply the rule to all incidents in the channel.

layers.description: Escalation levels in order. At least one level is required.

escalate_window.description: Wait before moving to the next level, in minutes.

force_escalate.description: When true, always escalate regardless of acknowledgement.

max_times.description: Max repeat notifications within the level.

target.description: Notification target. At least one of `person_ids`, `team_ids`, `schedule_to_role_ids`, or `emails` must be set, together with either `by` or `webhooks`.

critical.description: Notify channels used for Critical severity. Personal channels: `sms`, `voice`, `email`, `push`; IM group-chat channels: `feishu_app:<chat_id>`, `dingtalk_app:<chat_id>`, `wecom_app:<chat_id>`, `slack_app:<chat_id>`, `teams_app:<chat_id>`.

follow_preference.description: When true, use each responder's personal preference instead of the lists below.

info.description: Notify channels used for Info severity. Values as for `critical`.

warning.description: Notify channels used for Warning severity. Values as for `critical`.

person_ids.description: Member IDs to notify directly; obtain member IDs from `POST /member/list`.

schedule_to_role_ids.description: Map of schedule ID to the role IDs on that schedule to notify.

team_ids.description: Team IDs to notify; obtain team IDs from `POST /team/list`.

webhooks.description: Group chat / webhook targets. Required unless `by` is provided.

type.description: Webhook type, one of `feishu`, `feishu_app`, `dingtalk`, `dingtalk_app`, `wecom`, `slack`, `slack_app`, `teams_app`, `telegram`, `zoom`.

template_id.description: Notification template ID (MongoDB ObjectID).

time_filters.description: Optional recurring time windows during which the rule applies.

items.description: Recurring time window. `start`/`end` use 24-hour `HH:MM` format; `repeat` uses ISO-style weekday indices (0=Sunday … 6=Saturday).

cal_id.description: Optional calendar ID; restricts the window to days matching the calendar.

is_off.description: When true, match days marked as days-off in the calendar.

repeat.description: Days of the week this window repeats on. Empty means every day.

default_value.description: Optional default value. Type must match `field_type`: `bool` for checkbox; one of `options` for single_select; subset of `options` for multi_select; string ≤3000 chars for text.

display_name.description: Human-readable name. Must be unique within the account.

field_name.description: Machine name. Must start with a letter or underscore; 1–40 chars of `[a-zA-Z0-9_]`. Immutable after creation.

field_type.description:
Field type, immutable after creation.
| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `text` | Free text; `value_type` must be `string`, no `options`. |
| `single_select` | Single choice from `options`; `value_type` must be `string`. |
| `multi_select` | Multiple choices from `options`; `value_type` must be `string`. |
| `checkbox` | Boolean checkbox; `value_type` must be `bool`, no `options`. |

options.description: Required and non-empty for `single_select`/`multi_select` (unique strings, each 1–200 chars). Must be omitted or empty for `checkbox`/`text`.

value_type.description: Value type. `checkbox` requires `bool`; all other types require `string`. Immutable after creation. `float` is a reserved value currently rejected for every `field_type`.

field_id.description: Newly assigned field ID — 24-character hex ObjectID.

CreateIncidentCommentTypeRequest.description: Parameters for creating a comment type. At most 10 comment types per account.

color.description: Label color as a hex value in #RRGGBB format. Normalized to uppercase.

name.description: Display name. Trimmed before storing; must be unique within the account (case-insensitive). At most 40 characters.

CreateIncidentCommentTypeResponse.description: Result of creating a comment type.

comment_type_id.description: ID of the created comment type (24-character hex ObjectID).

CreateIncidentRequest.description: Parameters for manually creating an incident.

assigned_to.description: Incident assignment target. May be omitted entirely: when unset or empty, the channel's default assignment applies; required when the account's create form is in effect. `person_ids`, `escalate_rule_id`, and `emails` can be combined — responders are the union.

emails.description: Recipients to assign by email (1–100): resolved to account members and merged into `person_ids`; emails with no matching member are ignored.

escalate_rule_id.description: Escalation rule ID (MongoDB ObjectID); assigns the people at the rule's `layer_idx` layer.

layer_idx.description: Zero-based starting layer index of the escalation rule (default 0, the first layer); an out-of-range value returns an error. Only takes effect with `escalate_rule_id`.

notify.description: Override the notification channels used for this assignment.

follow_preference.description: When false, use `personal_channels`; when true or omitted, use each responder's personal preference.

template_id.description: Notification template ID (MongoDB ObjectID).

person_ids.description: Member IDs to assign directly (1–100). Can be combined with `escalate_rule_id`.

type.description:
Assignment type, derived server-side — callers do not set it: `assign` for manual creation, `reassign` for re-assignment, `escalate` for escalation-driven assignment.
| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `assign` | Initial assignment when the incident is created manually. |
| `reassign` | Re-assignment of an existing incident. |
| `escalate` | Assignment triggered by escalation policy advancement. |
| `reopen` | Assignment restarted from the first layer after the incident is reopened. |

channel_id.description: Channel to file the incident into. Optional; leave unset for a standalone incident.

fields.description: Custom field values keyed by field name. When a create form applies, only its visible fields are accepted.

CreateIncidentResponse.description: Result of manually creating an incident.

title.description: Echoes the incident title from the request.

CreateInhibitRuleRequest.description: Parameters for creating an inhibit rule.

channel_id.description: Owning channel ID; obtain it from `POST /channel/list`.

equals.description: Field keys whose values must be equal between the source (inhibiting) alert and the target (suppressed) alert, e.g. `data_source_id` or `labels.cluster`.

is_directly_discard.description: When true, matching alert events are discarded entirely; when false, alerts are still recorded but marked as muted by this rule.

source_filters.description: Conditions the source alert must match, evaluated against stored active alerts. Supported keys: `status`, `incident_status`, `alert_status`, `severity`, `incident_severity`, `alert_severity`, `title`, `description`, or any `labels.<name>`. Empty makes the rule inert.

target_filters.description: Conditions the incoming target alert event must match to be suppressed; empty means every event is a target.

CreateSilenceRuleRequest.description: Parameters for creating a silence rule. Exactly one of `time_filter` or `time_filters` must be provided, and `filters` must be non-empty.

channel_id.description: Owning channel ID; obtain it from `POST /channel/list`.

filters.description: Alert event match conditions (OR-of-AND). Required and must contain at least one condition.

from_incident_id.description: Incident ID (ObjectID hex) to attach the rule to. Optional; when set, only one enabled silence rule may exist per incident.

is_auto_delete.description: When true, the silence rule is automatically deleted after its time window expires. Defaults to false.

is_directly_discard.description: When true, matching alert events are discarded entirely; when false, alerts are still recorded but marked as muted by this rule.

time_filter.description: One-off time window defined by unix seconds.

end_time.description: Window end, Unix timestamp in seconds. Must be greater than 0.

start_time.description: Window start, Unix timestamp in seconds. Must be greater than 0 and less than `end_time`.

time_filters.description: Recurring time windows during which silencing applies. Mutually exclusive with `time_filter`.

items.description: Recurring time window. `start`/`end` use 24-hour `HH:MM` format; `repeat` uses ISO-style weekday indices (0=Sunday … 6=Saturday).

cal_id.description: Optional calendar ID; restricts the window to days matching the calendar.

is_off.description: When true, match days marked as days-off in the calendar.

repeat.description: Days of the week this window repeats on. Empty means every day.

CreateStatusPageChangeRequest.description: Parameters for creating a status page incident or maintenance event. The first update must contain `component_changes` to define affected components; retrospective events require at least 2 updates.

auto_update_by_schedule.description: Maintenance only: automatically advance the status based on the scheduled window.

close_at_seconds.description: Event close time in Unix seconds. Must be greater than or equal to the first update's `at_seconds`. For retrospective events this is the time the event ended; for maintenances with `auto_update_by_schedule` it schedules the automatic transition to `completed` and must be within 30 days from now.

description.description: Event description (Markdown). Must not be empty.

is_retrospective.description: Mark this event as a retrospective (historical) one.

linked_changes.description: Linked change IDs (related incidents, deployments, etc.).

notify_subscribers.description: Notify subscribers about this event and all its updates.

page_id.description: Status page ID; obtain it from `GET /status-page/list`.

responders.description: Member IDs responsible for the event.

start_at_seconds.description: Event start time in Unix seconds. The stored start time is always derived from the first update's `at_seconds` (which defaults to the current time when omitted); for maintenances with `auto_update_by_schedule`, this value schedules the automatic transition to `ongoing`.

status.description: Initial event status. `investigating`/`identified`/`monitoring`/`resolved` apply to incidents; `scheduled`/`ongoing`/`completed` apply to maintenances.

type.description: Change type: `incident` unplanned incident, `maintenance` planned maintenance.

updates.description: Timeline updates. At least one update is required, and at least one of them must contain `component_changes`. Immediate events normally pass one update; retrospective events must pass all historical updates.

items.description: One timeline update entry.

at_seconds.description: Update timestamp in Unix seconds. When omitted or 0 on the first update, defaults to the current time.

component_changes.description: Component status transitions applied by this update.

status.description: New component status. `operational`/`degraded`/`partial_outage`/`full_outage` apply to incidents; `operational`/`under_maintenance` apply to maintenances.

Change status after this update. May be omitted (or null) when the overall status does not change. The first four values apply to incident-type changes, the last three to maintenance-type changes.
| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `investigating` | Investigating (incident). |
| `identified` | Root cause identified (incident). |
| `monitoring` | Fix deployed, monitoring (incident). |
| `resolved` | Resolved (incident). |
| `scheduled` | Scheduled (maintenance). |
| `ongoing` | In progress (maintenance). |
| `completed` | Completed (maintenance). |

update_id.description: Update ID. Server-assigned on create; supply when replaying historical updates.

CreateStatusPageChangeTimelineRequest.description: Parameters for appending an update to a status page event timeline.

at_seconds.description: Update timestamp in Unix seconds. Defaults to the current time when omitted or 0.

change_id.description: Target change ID; obtain it from `GET /status-page/change/list`.

component_changes.description: Component status transitions applied by this update. Component IDs must be unique.

status.description: New component status. `operational`/`degraded`/`partial_outage`/`full_outage` apply to incidents; `operational`/`under_maintenance` apply to maintenances.

description.description: Update description (Markdown). Must not be empty.

page_id.description: Status page ID; obtain it from `GET /status-page/list`.

status.description:
Change status after this update; must be valid for the change type. When transitioning to `resolved` or `completed`, all affected components must be back to `operational`.
| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `investigating` | Investigating (incident). |
| `identified` | Root cause identified (incident). |
| `monitoring` | Fix deployed, monitoring (incident). |
| `resolved` | Resolved (incident). |
| `scheduled` | Scheduled (maintenance). |
| `ongoing` | In progress (maintenance). |
| `completed` | Completed (maintenance). |

CreateStatusPageDraftRequest.description: Parameters for storing a status page draft. The `draft` payload is stored verbatim; only the validated fields listed below are interpreted.

draft.description: Draft payload, stored verbatim, up to 64 KB serialized. contact_info.description: Get-in-touch contact, such as a mailto or website URL.

custom_domain.description: Custom domain for a public status page.

custom_links.description: Custom navigation links shown on the status page.

date_view.description: How change dates are displayed: `calendar` calendar view, `list` list view.

display_uptime_mode.description: Uptime display mode: `chart_and_percentage` chart plus percentage, `chart` chart only, `none` hidden.

name.description: Display name of the status page.

page_footer.description: Footer content shown on the status page.

page_header.description: Header content shown on the status page.

page_title.description: Browser title shown for the status page.

type.description: Visibility type: `public` accessible to anyone, `internal` restricted to logged-in members of this account.

url_name.description: URL-safe slug, unique per account and page type.

page_url_name.description: Final URL-safe slug assigned to the status page.

baseline_window.description: Baseline time window used by a comparison method.

window.description: Current analysis window using RFC 3339 UTC timestamps.

baseline_window.description: Baseline time window used by a comparison method.

methods.description: Diagnostic methods to run. When omitted, `log_patterns` defaults to `pattern_snapshot + pattern_compare(previous_window)` and `metric_trends` defaults to `single_window_shape + window_compare(previous_window)`.

baseline.description: Only meaningful for compare-style methods. operation.description: Diagnostic operation. When omitted, inferred from `ds_type` (loki / victorialogs → `log_patterns`, prometheus → `metric_trends`). Other sources must specify explicitly.

ErrorCode.description:
Flashduty error code enum. Every failed API response sets `error.code` to one of these stable wire strings. HTTP status is informational — the authoritative signal is the enum value.

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `OK` | 200 | Reserved — not returned on real errors. |
| `InvalidParameter` | 400 | A required parameter is missing or failed validation. |
| `BadRequest` | 400 | Generic 400 used when no more specific code fits. |
| `InvalidContentType` | 400 | The `Content-Type` header is not `application/json`. |
| `ResourceNotFound` | 400 | The referenced resource does not exist. Note: returned as HTTP 400, not 404 (historical choice). |
| `NoLicense` | 400 | The feature is license-gated and no active license was found. |
| `ReferenceExist` | 400 | Deletion blocked — other entities still reference this resource. |
| `Unauthorized` | 401 | `app_key` is missing, invalid, or expired. |
| `BalanceNotEnough` | 402 | Billing-gated operation with insufficient account balance. |
| `AccessDenied` | 403 | Authenticated but lacking the permission required for this operation. |
| `RouteNotFound` | 404 | The request URL path is not a known route. |
| `MethodNotAllowed` | 405 | The HTTP method is not allowed on this otherwise-known path. |
| `UndonedOrderExist` | 409 | An outstanding billing order blocks this new one. Wait and retry. |
| `RequestLocked` | 423 | Operation temporarily locked due to repeated failures. |
| `EntityTooLarge` | 413 | Request body exceeds the configured max size. |
| `RequestTooFrequently` | 429 | Rate limit hit — API-global, per-account, or per-integration. |
| `RequestVerifyRequired` | 428 | Second-factor verification required but not supplied. |
| `DangerousOperation` | 428 | High-risk operation requires MFA verification. |
| `InternalError` | 500 | Unhandled server-side error. Include `request_id` in the bug report. |
| `ServiceUnavailable` | 503 | A backend dependency is unavailable. Try again later. |

ErrorResponse.description: Response envelope for errors. `error` is required; `data` is absent.

request_id.description: Unique trace ID of this request; include it when reporting issues so logs can be located.

override.description: When `true`, overwrite the label if it already exists. Defaults to `false`.

result_label.description: Destination label key the composed value is written to. Must match `^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$`.

template.description: Go `text/template` string (1–500 characters) rendered against the event struct — e.g. `{{.Title}}`, `{{.Description}}`, `{{.Labels.key}}`. Example: `{{.Labels.region}}-{{.Labels.env}}`.

drop_labels.description: List of label keys to remove from the alert.

g_json.description: GJson path expression used to extract a value from a JSON-encoded field. Mutually exclusive with `pattern`.

override.description: When `true`, overwrite the label if it already exists. Defaults to `false`.

pattern.description: RE2 regular expression applied to the source value. Must contain at least one capture group; the captured groups are joined with a space and written to `result_label`. Mutually exclusive with `g_json`.

result_label.description: Destination label key the extracted value is written to. Must match `^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$`.

source_field.description: Source field to extract from. Must be `title`, `description`, or a label key prefixed with `labels.` (e.g. `labels.env`).

mapping_type.description: Mapping source type. `schema` uses a mapping schema table; `api` calls an external HTTP API.

override.description: When `true`, overwrite labels that already exist. Defaults to `false`.

result_labels.description: Label keys to populate from the mapping lookup result. Each must match `^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$`.

schema_id.description: Mapping schema ID (MongoDB ObjectID hex). Required when `mapping_type` is `schema`.

escalate_window.description: Wait before moving to the next level, in minutes.

force_escalate.description: When true, always escalate regardless of acknowledgement.

max_times.description: Max repeat notifications within the level.

created_at.description: Creation time, Unix timestamp in seconds.

deleted_at.description: Deletion time, Unix timestamp in seconds. Omitted unless the rule is soft-deleted; deleted rules are excluded from list responses.

filters.description: Incident-level match conditions (OR-of-AND tree): the rule is matched against the incident the alert was grouped into, not against the alert itself. Omit or leave empty to apply the rule to all incidents in the channel.

status.description: Rule status: `enabled` means active, `disabled` means paused, `deleted` is soft-deleted (possible only from the detail endpoint; lists never return deleted rules).

template_id.description: Notification template ID (MongoDB ObjectID).

time_filters.description: Recurring time windows during which the rule applies.

| `i_notify` | Notification dispatched through a channel at a specific escalation level. |
| `i_storm` | Alert storm threshold reached on the incident. |
| `i_snooze` | Notifications snoozed for a given duration. |
| `i_wake` | Snooze cancelled and notifications resumed. |
| `i_ack` | Acknowledged: Responder confirmed they are working on the incident. |
| `i_unack` | Acknowledgement removed. |
| `i_comm` | Comment: Responder logged progress or key information. |
| `i_rslv` | Resolved: Incident was marked as resolved. |
| `i_reopen` | Reopened: Resolved incident was reopened, possibly due to recurrence. |
| `i_merge` | Merged: Multiple related incidents were merged into one. |
| `i_r_title` | Title updated. |
| `i_r_desc` | Description updated. |
| `i_r_impact` | Impact updated. |
| `i_r_rc` | Root cause updated. |
| `i_r_rsltn` | Resolution updated. |
| `i_r_severity` | Severity Changed: Incident severity level was adjusted. |
| `i_r_field` | Custom field value updated. |
| `i_m_flapping` | Incident muted by flapping detection. |
| `i_m_reply` | Mute reply marker on a comment. |
| `i_custom` | Action: Automated action or script was triggered. |
| `i_wr_create` | War Room Created: Chat group was created for collaborative response. |
| `i_wr_delete` | War room chat group deleted. |
| `i_auto_refresh` | Card auto-refresh event posted back to the timeline. |
| `i_wi_created` | Work Item Created: An Action or Follow-up was created. |
| `i_wi_updated` | Work Item Updated: Title, description, status, or priority was changed. |
| `i_wi_assignees` | Work Item Assignees Changed: Assignees were updated. |
| `i_wi_completed` | Work Item Completed: An assignee marked the work item complete. |
| `i_wi_converted` | Work Item Converted: An Action was converted to a Follow-up. |
| `i_wi_bound` | Work Item Bound: A converted Follow-up was bound to a post-mortem. |
| `i_wi_deleted` | Work Item Deleted: An Action or Follow-up was soft-deleted. |
| `a_merge` | Alert Merged: An alert was merged into an existing incident. |

QueryDataRequest.description: Request for the stable structured query endpoint. It accepts the same query fields as the retired rows endpoint.

format.description: Public result-contract version. It is independent of the internal monit-edge query protocol version. Fixed at `query_result.v1`, which defines the structure of the `result` field.

QueryField.description: One typed column. `string` fields contain string or null values; `time` fields contain RFC 3339 Nano strings or null; `float` fields contain numbers, null, or the special strings `NaN`, `+Inf`, and `-Inf`.

labels.description: Series labels. Present on the float field of a time-series frame.

name.description: Column name; on a time-series float field, series are distinguished by `labels` and `name` is usually the metric name.

type.description: Value type governing `values` encoding: `string` = strings or null, `float` = numbers or `NaN`/`±Inf` strings or null, `time` = RFC 3339 Nano strings or null.

values.description: All values of this column in row order; length matches the other fields in the frame.

QueryFrame.description: A typed, columnar table or time-series frame. All fields in one frame have the same number of values. A `time_series` frame contains one time field and one float field; labels belong to the float field.

fields.description: Columns of the frame; all fields share the same `values` length and row i is composed of each field's `values[i]`.

kind.description: Frame type: `table` for a generic table, `time_series` for a series (exactly one time field and one float field).

frames.description: Typed table or time-series frames. A response can contain more than one frame.

kind.description: Result-kind discriminator, always `frames`, indicating the `frames` payload of typed table/time-series frames.
Result-kind discriminator, always `records`, indicating the `records` payload of schemaless record objects.

records.description: Schema-flexible records. Records may have different fields, contain nested JSON, or be null. Integers outside JavaScript's safe range are encoded as decimal strings.

QueryResult.description: Exactly one natural result shape, selected by `kind`.

account_id.description: Optional consistency check. Must equal the authenticated account when supplied; mismatched values are rejected. Business execution always uses the authenticated account.

args.description: Polymorphic key/value extension parameters forwarded verbatim to monit-edge. All values must be strings, and keys are always namespaced by source (e.g. `sls.project`, `loki.type`). Validation depends on `ds_type`: SLS requires `sls.project` + `sls.logstore`. Elasticsearch accepts `es.type` of `sql`, or omitted — any other value is rejected. Loki and VictoriaLogs accept `<source>.type` of `stats`, `raw`, or omitted; `raw` additionally requires a time range, either `<source>.start` + `<source>.end` or `<source>.timespan.value` + `<source>.timespan.unit` (unit one of `s`, `m`, `h`, `d`). Prometheus and the remaining SQL sources ignore `args` entirely.

delay_seconds.description: Look-back offset in seconds applied to point-in-time queries (Prometheus, Loki stats, VictoriaLogs stats). Ignored for raw / detail queries.

ds_name.description: Data source name; must match a configured data source under the tenant.

ds_type.description: Data source type; must match a configured data source under the tenant. Examples: `prometheus`, `loki`, `victorialogs`, `sls`, `elasticsearch`, `mysql`, `postgres`, `oracle`, `clickhouse`.

expr.description: Query expression. Syntax depends on `ds_type` and is interpreted by the corresponding monit-edge client (PromQL for Prometheus, LogQL for Loki, SQL for SQL sources, etc.).

labels.description: The sample's full label set; may be an empty object but is always present.

value.description: Finite numeric value or a JSON-safe representation of a non-finite float.

kind.description: Result-kind discriminator, always `samples`, indicating the `samples` payload of labeled instant samples.

samples.description: Instant samples with their complete label sets.

RemoteConfig.description: The whole per-application remote configuration. A change reaches an SDK asynchronously and is applied when that SDK creates its next session, so a running session never flips a decision mid-flight.

activation.description: How a change lands on a client that is already running: `next_session` (the default, and what an empty value means) leaves running sessions untouched and applies the change to new sessions; `immediate` ends the running session as soon as the change arrives so a new session starts under the new configuration.

custom.description: Application-defined pass-through values handed to the host app verbatim. At most 5 keys, each key up to 64 bytes, each value up to 4 KB of JSON nested at most 3 levels, 16 KB in total. Anyone holding the public client token can read it.

enabled.description: Kill switch. When false the engine reports no values at all and SDKs fall back to their init values.

refresh_on_foreground.description: Let clients re-check the configuration when they return to the foreground instead of waiting for the next poll.

rules.description: Targeting rules, evaluated in order; at most 20 per application.

content_hash.description: Hash of the configuration content; lets the console identify versions with identical content.

equivalent_to.description: Earliest version carrying the same content, when that is not this version itself.

reason.description: Operator's note left when the version was published. Empty when none was given.

updated_at.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds - when the version was published.

updated_by.description: ID of the member who published the version.

updated_by_name.description: Name of the member who published the version.

version.description: Version number, unique within the application.

RemoteConfigRule.description: One targeting rule: when `match` holds, `set` overrides `default`. The first matching rule wins and evaluation stops there - rule order is the priority.

match.description: Key/value conditions the SDK's config request must equal. Keys are limited to `env`, `app_version` and `sdk`; values are at most 256 bytes.

RemoteConfigValues.description: The SDK knobs a configuration can set. Every field is optional: a value absent from both rule and default is omitted from the SDK response, which tells the SDK to keep its init value.

defaultPrivacyLevel.description: How Session Replay masks a page by default.

traceSampleRate.description: Trace sampling rate (0-100): which sessions inject trace headers into their requests.

RouteCase.description: A single case branch in the routing rule. When all of its conditions match, the alert is dispatched to the configured channels.

channel_ids.description: Target channel IDs. Required when `routing_mode` is `standard` (or empty); returned as `null` for `name_mapping`.

fallthrough.description: If `true`, evaluation continues to the next case after this one matches; otherwise matching stops at the first hit.

if.description: List of match conditions that are AND-ed together.

name_mapping_label.description: Label key whose value is used as the target channel name. Required when `routing_mode` is `name_mapping`.

routing_mode.description: Routing mode. `standard` (default, also used when left empty) routes to the fixed channel IDs; `name_mapping` resolves channels by reading a label value from the alert event.

RouteDefault.description: Default branch used when no case matches (or all matched cases yield no valid channels).

channel_ids.description: Channel IDs to fall back to.

RouteInfoRequest.description: Parameters for retrieving the routing rule of one integration.

integration_id.description: Integration ID. Must be greater than 0.

RouteItem.description: Routing rule of an integration. Alerts are evaluated against `cases` in order; unmatched alerts fall through to `default`. Returns `null` when the integration has no configured rule.

created_at.description: Creation time, Unix timestamp in seconds.

creator_id.description: ID of the person who created the rule.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete timestamp, Unix seconds. Omitted when the rule is active.

integration_id.description: Integration the rule belongs to.

sections.description: Optional sections that visually group cases.

status.description: Route status. `enabled` means active; `deleted` means removed, visible only in historical versions.

updated_at.description: Last update time, Unix timestamp in seconds.

updated_by.description: ID of the person who performed the last update.

version.description: Monotonic version number, incremented on each update. Use it for optimistic concurrency control.

RouteMatchCondition.description: A single match condition. All conditions inside one case form an AND group.

key.description: Field key to match against the alert event (e.g. `alert_severity`, `labels.service`).

oper.description: Match operator. `IN` matches when the field value is one of `vals`; `NOTIN` matches when it is not.

vals.description: Values to compare against. Each value may be a literal string, a wildcard (`*`, `?`), a regular expression wrapped in slashes (`/pattern/`), a CIDR (`cidr:10.0.0.0/8`), or a numeric comparison (`num:lt:100`).

RouteSection.description: A logical section that groups consecutive cases for display purposes.

name.description: Section name. Must be unique within the rule.

position.description: Index in `cases` where this section starts. Must be between 0 and the length of `cases`.

RuleAuditListResponse.description: Audit records for a rule, ordered by creation time descending. The `content` field is omitted.

check_anydata.description: Any-data check configuration. Fires when the query returns any data rows.

alerting_check_times.description: Number of consecutive evaluations that must satisfy the condition before alerting; minimum 1.

enabled.description: Whether any-data checking is enabled: any returned data row triggers an alert.

push_recovery_event.description: Whether to push a recovery event notification when the alert resolves.

recovery.description: Recovery condition for any-data check. If omitted or `mode` is empty, treated as `nodata`.

args.description: Datasource-specific options for the recovery query, same convention as `queries[].args`; required for Elasticsearch datasources when `mode` is `ql`.

mode.description: `nodata` = recover when the query returns no data; `ql` = recover when the `condition` expression evaluates to true. When `mode` is `ql`, only a single query (`name=A`) is permitted.

recovery_check_times.description: Number of consecutive evaluations that must satisfy the recovery condition before resolving; minimum 1.

severity.description: Severity of any-data alert events; case-sensitive.

alert_on_empty_result.description: Whether to trigger an alert when every query returns an empty result.

alert_on_empty_result_severity.description: Severity of empty-result alerts, case-sensitive; only effective when `alert_on_empty_result` is enabled.

alerting_check_times.description: Number of consecutive evaluations that must satisfy the condition before alerting; minimum 1.

enabled.description: Whether no-data checking is enabled: a previously-seen series that stops returning data triggers an alert.

push_recovery_event.description: Whether to push a recovery event notification when the alert resolves.

recovery_check_times.description: Number of consecutive evaluations that must satisfy the recovery condition before resolving; minimum 1.

severity.description: Severity of no-data alert events; case-sensitive.

alerting_check_times.description: Number of consecutive evaluations that must satisfy the condition before alerting; minimum 1.

critical.description: Critical threshold expression referencing query results via `$<query>` or `$<query>.<value_field>`, e.g. `$A > 90`; at least one severity must be configured.

enabled.description: Whether threshold checking is enabled.

info.description: Info threshold expression, same syntax as `critical`.

push_recovery_event.description: Whether to push a recovery event notification when the alert resolves.

recovery.description: Recovery evaluation configuration for threshold checks.

args.description: Datasource-specific extra parameters for the recovery query, using the same `<datasource>.<param>` key convention as query `args`. Omitted when empty.

condition.description: Recovery condition expression; required when `mode` is `threshold` or `ql`, and must be empty for `invert`.

mode.description: Recovery mode: `invert` = resolve when the alert expression no longer holds (`condition` stays empty); `threshold` = resolve when the `condition` threshold expression holds; `ql` = resolve when the `condition` query expression evaluates true.

value_fields.description: Numeric result fields the recovery `condition` references as `$A.<field>`; same semantics as the query's `value_fields`. Omitted when empty.

recovery_check_times.description: Number of consecutive evaluations that must satisfy the recovery condition before resolving; minimum 1.

warning.description: Warning threshold expression, same syntax as `critical`.

queries.description: Query list with at least one entry; each needs a unique `name` (`R` and `__all__` are reserved) and a non-empty, non-duplicate `expr`.

args.description: Datasource-specific query options keyed by the `<datasource>.<option>` convention (e.g. `es.type`, `tencent_cls.limit`); most datasources need none.

label_fields.description: Result fields that become alert event labels — identical label sets collapse into one alert; must not overlap `value_fields`; applies to table-shaped results (SQL/ES-style datasources).

name.description: Query identifier (letter, e.g. `A`). The name `R` is reserved and must not be used.

value_fields.description: Numeric result fields used in threshold evaluation (referenced as `$A.<field>` in threshold expressions); required for threshold checks unless the datasource is `prometheus`/`loki`/`victorialogs`; field names must not contain `.`.

relate_queries.description: Optional auxiliary queries whose results are attached to alert events as context. Each entry must have a unique `name` (not duplicating any query name) and a non-empty `expr`.

args.description: Datasource-specific options for the auxiliary query, same convention as `queries[].args`.

RuleCounterChannelResponse.description: Map of channel name to rule count. Unresolved channel IDs appear as stringified IDs.

RuleCounterNodeResponse.description: Map of top-level folder name to rule count.

RuleCounterTotalResponse.description: Historical rule-count samples ordered by `clock` ascending.

rule_name.description: Rule name echoed back from the request.

RuleDsTypesResponse.description: Datasource types available to the account — global types plus account-scoped types.

annotations.description: Annotation key-value pairs delivered with alert events; keys must not start with `$` (reserved for query fields). Effective only when `fields` includes `annotations`.

annotations_patch.description: Partial annotation update. Effective only when `fields` includes `annotations`; takes precedence over `annotations` when both are sent.

channel_ids.description: IDs of the collaboration spaces alerts are sent to; may be empty. Effective only when `fields` includes `channel_ids`.

cron_pattern.description: Schedule expression: a 6-field cron (with seconds) or an `@every 30s` interval descriptor; `CRON_TZ=`/`TZ=` prefixes are not allowed. Effective only when `fields` includes `cron_pattern`.

debug_log_enabled.description: Whether to enable debug logging; the edge emits detailed evaluation logs for troubleshooting. Effective only when `fields` includes `debug_log_enabled`.

delay_seconds.description: Seconds to shift the evaluation query window backward, compensating for data ingestion latency. Effective only when `fields` includes `delay_seconds`.

description.description: Rule description (Markdown). Effective only when `fields` includes `description`.

ds_ids.description: Datasource IDs, merged with `ds_list` to decide which datasources the rule monitors; IDs survive datasource renames. Effective only when `fields` includes `ds_ids`.

ds_list.description: Datasource name match patterns; wildcards supported. Effective only when `fields` includes `ds_list`.

ds_type.description: Datasource type identifier; allowed values are listed by `POST /monit/rule/dstypes`. Effective only when `fields` includes `ds_type`.

enabled.description: Whether the rule is enabled. Setting it to `false` makes the server clean up the rule's active alerts. Effective only when `fields` includes `enabled`.

enabled_times.description: Time windows during which the rule is in effect; element structure see `EnabledTime`. Effective only when `fields` includes `enabled_times`.

fields.description: Field names to update. Only listed fields are updated, taking new values from the same-named request fields; values for unlisted fields are silently ignored.

labels.description: Custom label key-value pairs; replaces existing labels as a whole. Effective only when `fields` includes `labels`.

labels_patch.description: Partial label update. Effective only when `fields` includes `labels`; takes precedence over `labels` when both are sent.

repeat_interval.description: Interval in seconds between repeated alert notifications. Effective only when `fields` includes `repeat_interval`.

repeat_total.description: Maximum number of repeated notifications. Effective only when `fields` includes `repeat_total`.

timezone.description: Timezone in which the rule executes. IANA timezone name; defaults to `Asia/Shanghai`.

id.description: Alert rule ID. Obtainable per folder via `POST /monit/rule/list/basic`.

RuleImportRequest.description: Array of alert rule export objects to import.

RuleListRequest.description: Filter parameter for listing rules in a folder.

folder_id.description: Folder ID. Must be an existing folder; `0` is rejected with a `folder_not_found` error.

include_descendants.description: Also include rules from all descendant folders. When `true`, each returned item carries only `id`, `folder_id` and `name`; combine with `query` / `limit` for rule-picker scenarios.

limit.description: Max number of rules returned; only effective when `include_descendants` is `true`. Defaults to 50, capped at 100.

query.description: Rule name fuzzy filter; only effective when `include_descendants` is `true`.

channel_ids.description: Channel IDs to send alerts to. Used only when `delivery_mode` is `oncall`.

delivery_mode.description: Alert delivery channel: `oncall` routes alert events through Flashduty On-call, `webhook` POSTs them directly to `webhook_url`. An empty value is treated as `oncall`, and on create/update it is persisted as the deployment default (`webhook` on RUM-only on-premises deployments, `oncall` otherwise). Omitted when empty (legacy rows).

enabled.description: Whether alerting is enabled.

integration_id.description: Associated on-call integration ID (read-only, auto-assigned on save when `delivery_mode` is `oncall`).

webhook_url.description: URL that receives alert events when `delivery_mode` is `webhook`; required in that mode, ignored otherwise. Omitted when empty.
